skill.name: readme
skill.description: Generate comprehensive README.md documentation for a project, including setup, architecture, environment variables, scripts, testing, deployment, and troubleshooting guidance.
skill.summary: Creates detailed README.md files from project context.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most command findings are false positives from Markdown examples, not executable skill code. The remaining concerns involve credential-file guidance and a self-declared risk label that could mislead review. The author should remove safety claims and avoid directing agents or users to inspect master keys.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the risk: safe front matter or replace it with neutral metadata that does not claim an audit result.
Change exploration guidance to inspect only sample files and never read config/master.key, encrypted credentials, or real env files.
Replace cat config/master.key and similar examples with secret-manager guidance and platform-specific secure variable setup.
Label sudo and rm examples as user-run troubleshooting steps and require confirmation before any agent executes commands.

content.value_statement: Project READMEs often miss setup, architecture, and deployment details. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to inspect a project and draft a complete README.
actual_capabilities: Generates a README outline with overview, features, tech stack, prerequisites, and setup steps.
Documents architecture, directory structure, request flow, data flow, and major components.
Lists environment variables, common scripts, testing commands, deployment paths, and troubleshooting steps.
Adapts deployment sections for Docker, Kamal, Heroku, Fly.io, Render, or similar platforms.
Writes the finished README.md content directly into the project root when used as instructed.
limitations: Accuracy depends on the project files available to the agent.
Several examples are Rails focused and may need adaptation for other stacks.
The skill references credential files, so users should restrict access to real secrets.
It does not verify commands or deployment settings unless the user asks for validation.

use_cases.title: Document a New Repository
use_cases.description: Create a complete README for a project that has little or no documentation.

use_cases.title: Improve Team Onboarding
use_cases.description: Expand setup, architecture, and testing notes so new engineers can start faster.

use_cases.title: Prepare Release Documentation
use_cases.description: Add deployment, environment, and troubleshooting sections before a production handoff.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Starter README
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a README.md for this project. Include overview, prerequisites, setup, scripts, testing, and troubleshooting.

prompt_templates.title: Update Existing Documentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current README.md and update missing setup, environment, and testing details from the repository.

prompt_templates.title: Document Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the project structure and add architecture, data flow, major components, and deployment guidance to the README.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Production Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite the README for production maintainers. Include deployment options, required configuration, operational checks, and known failure modes.

output_examples.input: A Rails project with a minimal README.
output: Expanded README with setup, architecture, environment variables, scripts, testing, deployment, and troubleshooting sections.
Clear notes explain what each setup step does and where project files live.

output_examples.input: A repository with Docker, tests, and deployment config.
output: README includes Docker setup, local development commands, test workflow, deployment notes, and operational troubleshooting.
The structure helps a new contributor run and understand the project.

best_practices: Review generated credential guidance before publishing documentation.
Confirm setup and deployment commands on a clean environment.
Keep examples specific to the detected stack and remove irrelevant sections.
anti_patterns: Do not include real secrets, tokens, or master keys in generated documentation.
Do not document commands that were not checked against the repository.
Do not use generic Rails sections when the project uses another framework.

faq.question: Does this skill run project commands?
faq.answer: No. It guides the agent to inspect project context and write README content; command execution depends on the host agent.

faq.question: Can it update an existing README?
faq.answer: Yes. It can expand or rewrite an existing README when the file is available.

faq.question: Which projects fit best?
faq.answer: It fits web applications, APIs, libraries, and internal tools that need developer setup documentation.

faq.question: Does it handle deployment docs?
faq.answer: Yes. It looks for deployment indicators and adds relevant deployment guidance.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use sample values and secret-manager references. Do not include real keys, tokens, or production connection strings.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
